articleMarkdown:
# Studying Jiǎn (Obstruction): finding a workable path when the way is blocked

When a route will not work, identify the obstacle, adjust the approach, and seek help that can supply what is actually missing.

Continuing forward does not necessarily bring the goal closer. Jiǎn repeatedly describes going and coming, moving among obstruction, return, connection, and the arrival of friends. It helps separate commitment from route: even when a goal retains its value, the method may need to change.

## Identity and line order

Jiǎn is hexagram 39 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with symbol ䷦. The lower trigram is Gèn ☶ and the upper trigram is Kǎn ☵; their traditional images are mountain and water, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初六、六二、九三、六四、九五、上六. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line labels designate yang and yin; they are not additional line numbers.

```text
━━━━ ━━━━  上六
━━━━━━━━━  九五
━━━━ ━━━━  六四
━━━━━━━━━  九三
━━━━ ━━━━  六二
━━━━ ━━━━  初六
```

## Hexagram statement

蹇：利西南，不利東北；利見大人，貞吉。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Obstruction: the southwest is favorable, the northeast unfavorable. It is beneficial to meet a great person; steadfast correctness brings good fortune.

Legge explains Jiǎn as difficult movement, dividing the response into conditions such as location, helpers, and steadfast correctness. Southwest and northeast belong to traditional imagery and interpretation, not direct instructions for travel, relocation, or choosing a direction.

Today, ask exactly where the difficulty lies, who has relevant experience, and which conditions need to change before acting. This is more specific than simply demanding greater effort from yourself.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Interpretations in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images belong to the commentarial collection known as the Yìzhuàn, usually called the Ten Wings. Below, these commentaries are kept separate from the hexagram and line statements, followed by modern learning applications.

The Commentary on the Judgment explicitly describes danger ahead and calls recognizing danger and stopping wise. The Commentary on the Images takes water above a mountain and speaks of self-examination and cultivation of conduct. Stopping and examining oneself do not signify an inability to act.

Today, self-examination can test your assumptions and methods without turning every external obstacle into a character defect. Acknowledging limits in resources or institutions is also part of understanding the situation.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [hon-sep](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/chinese-change/)

## The six lines, from bottom to top

### 初六 · When the original route is blocked, pause first

往蹇，來譽。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Going meets obstruction; returning earns praise.

Legge reads the first line as advance increasing difficulty and staying back receiving approval. This judgment depends on circumstances; it is not a general celebration of retreat.

When essential information is missing, clarifying the problem may be more effective than repeated submissions or forcing entry. Waiting should aim to supply conditions, not suspend everything indefinitely.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六二 · Serve shared concerns while recognizing limits to responsibility

王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: The king's minister meets obstruction upon obstruction, not for personal reasons.

The king's minister faces repeated difficulty for more than personal reasons. Legge retains the sense of public duty. Ancient ruler-minister relations cannot require unlimited sacrifice from people today.

If you take on extra work for a shared aim, explain the necessary support and scope. An unselfish motive does not automatically make an overloaded arrangement reasonable.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九三 · Returning can create reconnection

往蹇來反。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Going meets obstruction; coming brings return.

Legge reads coming back as stopping the advance and returning to former companions. It does not mean erasing every gain already made.

After an attempt fails, return to actual users or collaborators and ask what did not meet their needs. The value of return lies in new information, not merely renewed familiarity.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六四 · Turn isolated efforts into coordinated action

往蹇來連。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Going meets obstruction; coming brings connection.

Coming into connection adds joining to mere return. Legge understands it through assistance and ancient relations of duty.

If a task needs several people, first explain the interdependent parts. Specific requests make it easier to establish what is needed, instead of vaguely hoping someone will solve everything for you.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九五 · A major difficulty need not rest on one person

大蹇朋來。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Great obstruction; friends arrive.

Serious difficulty and friends arriving to help appear together. Legge explains this through a shared response. It does not promise that real help will arrive automatically.

Describe the difficulty proactively to trustworthy, capable people and establish which part they can help with. A good relationship does not mean unlimited resources; assistance should fit the other person's capacity and willingness.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 上六 · A revised arrangement may yield more

往蹇來碩，吉；利見大人。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Going meets obstruction; coming brings something greater. Good fortune; it is beneficial to meet a great person.

Legge reads coming to greatness as a larger result from not pressing ahead rashly, again emphasizing meeting a great person. This gain belongs to the selected traditional interpretation, not a forecast of wealth.

After changing routes, test whether obstacles have actually decreased and understanding increased. Suitable guidance should have a checkable basis; calling someone an expert does not exempt them from questions.

References: [zhouyi-39](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/蹇&oldid=2405036), [legge1882-39](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Finding help with an unfamiliar task

Original modern scenario

An organizer takes over a collection of documents and repeatedly classifies them according to her own understanding, yet others still cannot find things. She pauses the rearrangement, asks actual users how they search, and invites someone familiar with the material to identify key fields with her.

Using that feedback, she narrows the trial, makes one part of the collection genuinely usable, then decides how to expand. Material nobody can yet explain keeps a verification-pending marker.

Jiǎn here turns difficulty into a clue for changing the method. A temporary obstacle does not establish incompetence, and seeking help does not replace one's own responsibility.

## Misreadings to avoid

- Jiǎn's difficult movement is not a basis for judging people with physical disabilities or predicting lifelong obstruction. Directions and divinatory judgments cannot replace practical planning.

- Seeking help does not require unconditional obedience to authority. Important health, legal, financial, and safety judgments require relevant facts and professional support.

## Three practices

1. Describe the obstacle as a specific missing condition, rather than merely saying you cannot do it.

2. Identify someone who may supply one missing condition and prepare a clear question.

3. Set an observable criterion for testing whether the new route works better.

## Related hexagram

### Jiě — Deliverance (hexagram-40)

Jiǎn considers adjustment when blocked; Jiě considers action after the blockage loosens. Once an opening is found, identify which work can end and which still needs completion.

## A closing question

While reading Jiǎn, ask: is it the aim itself that deserves persistence, or a route I have become unwilling to re-examine?
